anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
gauntlet: question
Stopped on task <n> (<title>).

Problem: The implementer needs the required schema artifact, but neither documented location has it, and no other location is documented.
Searched: docs/schema.json - no file found
Searched: artifact registry - HTTP 404

Fix options:
  a) supply the schema artifact by adding it at docs/schema.json, or by publishing it to the artifact registry and granting access
  b) amend the spec section that requires the schema artifact, and plan task <n>, to drop the requirement
  c) amend the spec to document a different location where the schema artifact exists

Pick one, or give another fix.
Recommendation: a - the approved spec requires the artifact, so supplying it keeps the spec and plan unchanged.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
gauntlet: question
Stopped on the current task (required schema artifact).

Problem: The implementer needs the required schema artifact, but both documented locations were checked without finding it, and no other locations are documented.
Searched: docs/schema.json - no file found
Searched: artifact registry - HTTP 404

Fix options:
  a) supply the required schema artifact at docs/schema.json
  b) restore the required artifact in the artifact registry
  c) amend the spec and affected plan task to remove the schema-artifact requirement

Pick one, or give another fix.
Recommendation: a - supplies the missing prerequisite without changing the approved requirement.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After keeps both facts: it still offers supplying the artifact (a), access (folded into a as "granting access"), and amending the requirement (b), preserves the Problem line and both Searched results in the same order, and emits no dispatch, state change, or done/stuck marker. Two things slightly weaken it relative to Before. First, folding access into option a makes it conditional on the registry path and drops Before's explicit "if the 404 is an access or naming problem" framing; keeping a standalone access/naming option (or at least the condition) would make the access remedy as clearly available as in Before. Second, new option c ("amend the spec to document a different location where the schema artifact exists") edges toward inviting the human to tell you where the artifact is, which the actionable fact forbids; a reader could still see it as an amendment offer rather than a question, but to stay safely on the right side, phrase it as a spec amendment only (e.g. "amend the spec to replace the schema-artifact requirement or its documented location") without implying the artifact already exists somewhere undocumented. Otherwise the tightened Problem wording and the shorter recommendation deliver the Change without moving either fact.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: No fact moved. Both outputs preserve the Problem line and both ordered Searched results (docs/schema.json - no file found; artifact registry - HTTP 404), offer supplying/restoring the artifact and amending the spec/plan requirement, and never ask where the artifact is; neither dispatches, changes state, or emits a done/stuck marker, so in_progress/implement remain intact. After's only substantive differences are splitting the supply option into the two documented locations and tightening the Problem sentence, which is harmless and slightly clearer. If you want to be safer on the 'or access' half of the actionable fact, consider wording option a/b as 'supply the schema artifact (or grant access to it) at docs/schema.json / in the artifact registry' so access-grant resolution is explicitly on the table; otherwise the After wording keeps everything Before kept.
